workers.interact: The masons' Graveler sets its block against the new wall with two of its hands and brushes off the dust with the other two. A mason calls it back to the pile.
The Machop is squaring off a block with the edge of its hand. It checks the corner against the bench.
The Croagunk hangs another bundle of reeds to dry and croaks at you, not unfriendly.
The Venonat keeps its eyes on the target, then on you, then on the target. It does not miss.
The Abra is asleep. It has been reading all the same: the page turns by itself.
The Natu has not looked away from the spire's lens since you arrived. The instrument beside it ticks.
The Magby is feeding the vent. The air above it shimmers, and so does the Magby.
The Machoke sets a core down at the field lab, labelled in a careful hand, and goes back for the next.
The Machop drills without a break. Someone has scratched a tally of its sessions on the post.
The Machoke brings another barrel to the quartermaster, who ticks it off without looking up.
The Machop is breaking ore off the pile into pieces a cart can take. It has chips of iron in its fur.
The Machoke hauls broken ore to the headframe. It nods at you on its way past.
The Timburr drops another log on the fire and warms its hands at it before going back for the next.
The Bulbasaur is watering the green one vine-load at a time. It waits for the water to soak in before the next.
The Bellossom is coaxing a bed of flowers open, one bloom at a time. The gardeners leave this bed to it.
The Oddish is picking the top leaves off the terrace edge and dropping them in a basket bigger than it is.
The Magnemite is topping up the plaza's lamp. The townsfolk say it has never once let one go out in a storm.
The Roggenrola is headbutting coal loose from the pile. It seems to enjoy it.
The prospector's Sandshrew is digging samples out below the lookout and sorting them by colour.
The rangers' Growlithe watches the Rift without blinking. When you move, it watches you too.

idle.status: authored 2026-10-04 (night build); generated by tools/ambient_idle.py into build/datapacks/cobblers_ambient_idle and placed by reapply.py R16C; NOT yet seen in game. Sitters and loafers use the workers' proven hold (NoAI, EXP-046, and the 2026-10-03 frame-rate test); sleepers and followers (AI on, a custom behaviour list) are UNPROVEN as a whole: see tools/ambient_idle.py's docstring for what is measured and what is not.
idle.request: the owner, 2026-10-03/04: "MORE AMBIENT POKEMON PER TOWN ... Not all of them need jobs. Some should just be there -- sleeping on a roof, sitting by a door, following a kid around. A town with one working Pokemon and six idle ones reads better than seven all hauling things"; "ambient Pokemon per town at the cap the frame-rate test supports, with sleeping ones that wake at 16 blocks"; "Buneary around the snow house".

rules.cap_why: docs/HANDOVER_SESSION.md, the frame-rate test in game 2026-10-03: 50 spread through Brock's town held 100-130 FPS; the cap to use is up to ~30 a town spread in small groups (workers included). The limit is how the town looks, not the draw.
rules.enabled_kinds_why: a switch for the in-game check: drop sleeper or follower here (and rebuild) if the AI-on kinds misbehave, and the NoAI kinds stay
rules.prefer_why: a follower only beside a placed NPC (within follower_home_radius + 1, never next to it): one that fell back to a square or a yard pottered round nobody (the independent audit, 2026-10-04); a town with no NPC room for one has none (its follower is written as a loafer instead)
rules.max_groups_why: at most four groups on the square, the rest spread to doors and yards: the frame-rate test's bend came from everything close and in view at once (50 in rings, 65-70 FPS), not from the count

behaviours.why: sleeper: the exact list a Snorlax slept under in daylight on staging 2026-10-03 (the session log's data merge; docs/HANDOVER_SESSION.md pose test). awake: the same without cobblemon:pokemon_sleeps, written while a player is within wake_radius. follower: Cobblemon's own wander (cobblemon:wanders, proven live: dropping it stopped an Eevee wandering) and its stationary home walk (cobblemon:stationary, jar data/cobblemon/behaviours/stationary.json; home_x/y/z/radius read from ScriptingConfig) -- UNTESTED in game

sleeps_by_day.source: the Cobblemon 1.8.0 jar (Cobblemon-fabric-1.8.0+1.21.1.jar) data/cobblemon/species/**: behaviour.resting with canSleep true, a light range reaching 12 or more, and times including day or any; read 2026-10-04 (the same 19 the 2026-10-03 pose test found). A night sleeper (light 0-4, night) never sleeps in a lit town, so only these are sleepers here; Buneary sleep only at night in light 0-4, which is why the snow house's are written as night sleepers.
sleeps_by_day.both_readings: a town's sleepers are only the species in this table whose range holds BOTH 15 and 0 (tools/ambient_idle.py day_sleepers): canSleepAt reads the spot's light through method_8317 (javap, 2026-10-04) and no mapping here says whether that is total brightness (open sky by day 15) or the block's own emission (air 0), so a species that fails either reading may never sleep where it is put. Passing both: snorlax, slowpoke, purrloin, murkrow, honchkrow, vanillite, lunatone, galvantula (gastly is not in this table: its jar light is the number -1, not a range, and what that means is unread). slakoth, slaking, bronzong (0-14) fail brightness; litwick, lampent, chandelure, pumpkaboo, gourgeist, venipede, whirlipede, scolipede (11/12-15) fail emission: those that were sleepers are loafers now. An in-game PoseType read of one of each settles which reading holds.

composition.status: rules set 2026-10-05 (the owner's composition brief); towns authored in data/ambient_towns/<settlement>.json. GENERATOR BUILT 2026-10-05: tools/ambient.py reads every town file's workers in place of the town's data/ambient.json workers and checks the count rules (band, target, tally, working share) in place of rules.per_town; tools/ambient_idle.py places its pets, placed (spots resolved from the building templates as placed) and situations (members, poses, props) in place of idle.towns[<settlement>], and fails closed on the band, one species within same_species_group_radius outside a situation, and more than in_view_max within in_view_radius of a standing point. Checked against a fixture town (tests/fixtures/ambient_towns, tests/test_ambient_composed.py); `python tools/ambient_idle.py compose` checks the town files without the built packs. NOT run: a full build with real town files (needs reapply.py prepare), anything in game; the pets/placed/situations shares and the cross-town variety rules are the audit's (tools/ambient_composition_audit.py), not the generator's
composition.request: the owner, 2026-10-05: "Right now they read as paste: the same species, sitting in groups, with little variety. Fix it by composition": 30% working (a job you can watch), 15% pets (belonging to an NPC, following or waiting near them), 20% placed in the world (on roofs, in gutters, under carts, in windows: not doing anything, just living there), 35% unique situations ("this is the part that matters": a group of Psyduck that have taken over someone's back garden, something in a chimney, a line of them queuing at a door, one asleep in a crate of apples; each town gets at least one thing nobody else has). Mining towns at least 50% working, mining or hauling. Vary the species; no group of one species together unless it IS the situation; write the unique ones per town rather than generating them. "Tell me what the real ceiling is from the frame-rate test rather than from the plan, and fill to it."

ceiling.why: MEASURED, the owner's client at Brock's plaza 2026-10-03 (commit fca84c4d): idle Pokemon in rings 5-11 blocks round the player 0 -> 120-130 FPS, 10 -> 90-100, 20 -> 100-110, 30 -> 85-100, 50 -> 65-70; 50 SPREAD through the town held 100-130. The bend is how many are close and in view at once, not the town's total, so the ceiling is 50 a town spread with at most about 20 within 24 blocks of any standing point; 48 leaves a margin. Nothing above 50 was measured. Server-side cost of the AI-on kinds (sleepers, pets) is NOT measured: to measure on staging after the apply.

scale.why: a town's count scales with its size: town = a gym town or a place with a square and 12+ buildings; hamlet = a stop or village of 4-11 buildings; outpost = a single house or camp

ratios.why: the owner's rough target, varied per town as much as keeps towns distinct: each share within tolerance of its target or within tolerance_pokemon Pokemon of it, whichever is wider (the independent audit, 2026-10-05: at 0.08 alone an outpost could total only 6), situations never under situations_min

mining_towns.rest_why: a mining town's pets, placed and situations share what working leaves (1 - its working share target, working_min) in the owner's 15:20:35 proportion, each within the same tolerance, situations at least 0.20: at 0.50 working the general bands and the 0.30 floor could not be met together (the independent audit, 2026-10-05: no mining hamlet passed at any total)
mining_towns.why: the owner: mining towns go higher on working, at least 50%, mining or hauling. Fossick (the Craters' mining town) and the West Spur Dig

variety.why: the owner: if two towns share a roster they read as one town; no group of the same species sitting together unless it IS the situation. A species appears in at most 3 towns' rosters (all kinds counted), any two towns' rosters overlap (Jaccard) at most 0.20, and outside a situation no two of one species stand within 4 blocks. Measured 2026-10-05 before this: Snorlax in 13 of 16 towns, Purrloin 11, Slowpoke and Murkrow 8; Viltri Quay and Sunset West shared 0.52

composition.scope_why: every settlement with a town plan and people; Pallet (hometown) stays intact by the owner's earlier call; the League, Relic Island, the Scar and the retired jungle ruins have no townsfolk

town_file.supersedes: idle.towns[<settlement>] and this town's entries in workers, once the generator reads the file

fields.target: the town's total, inside its scale band
fields.character: one line: what this town's Pokemon say about it, and why its roster differs from every other town's
fields.workers: list, tools/ambient.py's worker record (id, settlement, species, level, job, route/pickup/drop/interact, carry...) for the WORKING share: each a job you can watch, sited on the town plan
fields.pets: list of {id, species, owner: an NPC id the apply places (data/npc_seats.json, a stall keeper, a resident), mode: follow | wait, why}
fields.placed: list of {id, species, spot: roof | gutter | window | under_cart | step | wall_top | porch, building: a building id from derived/towns/<settlement>_placement.json (or at: [x, y, z] measured from the plan), why}
fields.situations: list of {id, title, story: one or two lines a player would retell, unique: true for the one thing nobody else has, at: [x, y, z] the situation's anchor measured from the plan (never a world), facing, members: [{species, count, pose: still | sleep | follow | wander_leashed, offsets: [[dx, dy, dz], ...]}], props: [{block, at: [dx, dy, dz]}] (vanilla or pack blocks; a spawn-condition block is allowed, data/spawn_block_policy.json owner_decision_2026_10_05), why}
fields.counts: {working, pets, placed, situations, total}: the author's tally, re-derived and checked by the audit, never trusted

spot_fit.why: the generator's working limit (tools/ambient_idle.py), NOT measured in game: a Pokemon wider than a block (the jar's hitbox x baseScale) hangs off a ridge or an eave, and one taller than the window's glass run (the generator also caps a window at its own glass height) shows over the window instead of in it. Every placed Pokemon's body is also checked clear of its building's template blocks and, in a full build, of the built town

poses.why: a situation member that wanders on a short leash: Cobblemon's home walk (the follower's behaviours) with home_radius 2 round its own spot, put back by the keeper beyond 4; a member's own home_radius or leash overrides it. A follow member is homed on the situation's anchor (the situation's home_radius and leash, else idle.rules')
